newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Upper House passes extra budget for 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan Upper House passes extra budget for 96/97.

text.p: Japan's Upper House of parliament on Friday approved a supplementary budget totalling 2.67 trillion yen for the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31.
The Lower House passed the extra budget on Wednesday.
The ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) got the measure passed with the help of two parties with which it has formed a loose policy alliance.
The three main opposition parties had called for revisions to the budget including changes in its priorities and reductions in some spending, but the LDP rejected the demands.
The extra budget will fund the rehabilitation of areas around Kobe in western Japan, hit by a massive earthquake in 1995, and measures to help cope with natural disasters.

It will also cover the costs of a serious food poisoning outbreak during the summer and measures taken to cushion farmers after a global trade agreement in 1993 liberalised farm trade. The budget also includes provisions related to the scaling back of U.S. military bases in Okinawa.
The government plans to issue about 1.34 trillion yen worth of bonds to fund the extra budget.
